title: CAM-117 Half B: plan-runner gates + BLOCK->re-plan loop + escalation
description: Part 2 of CAM-117 (deterministic plan-runner). Half A delivers the runner skeleton + planner/auditor worker-pane spawn + file-based handback + happy-path auto-mode (APPROVE -> commit PRD + branch + flip active:true); on auditor BLOCK it escalates to the operator with no auto re-plan. Half B adds the gates/escalation cluster: (1) deterministic BLOCK->re-plan loop (re-spawn planner with the auditor findings, cap N=2 rounds, escalate to operator on non-convergence, never infinite-loop; mirrors loop.ts FIXES_PENDING->re-implement + MAX_ROUNDS terminal); (2) plan_approval=operator gate that reviews the FULL audited PRD (pause + notify orchestrator + wait for explicit approval, then commit+flip); (3) in-progress-work conflict detection (prd.json with passes:false, or on a cam/* branch) escalated to operator (continue/ship/abandon), never auto-decided; (4) reduce cam-plan.md to a thin phase-signal (control-flow now in TS). Depends on CAM-117 Half A. Split done on engineering merit per CAM-117 spec gotcha #6 + prd-size-vs-review-convergence lesson.

spec.scope: Half B of CAM-117: convert the plan phase into a LIVE deterministic sidecar-driven runner (Half A shipped the inert runPlanPhase skeleton). Sidecar-driven: a `phase` enum in .claude/cam-loop.local.md becomes the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the loop phase (idle|planning|implementing|awaiting-operator|shipping); the existing `active` bool is DERIVED from `phase === 'implementing'` (all readActive/outer-loop consumers read the derived value). `cam plan N` writes `phase: planning` + the issue id; the sidecar outer loop detects it and invokes runPlanPhase, mirroring how `active:true` drives the implement loop today. On auditor APPROVE + plan_approval=auto, runPostAuditAction commits the PRD + creates the branch + flips `phase: implementing` (the existing loop.ts assumes implement->review->ship). Adds: (1) a deterministic BLOCK->re-plan loop: the runner reads the auditor findings from plan-verdict-report.json and INJECTS them into the re-spawned planner's prompt (mirrors the CAM-37 review-findings->fix-story propagation), capped at 2 rounds (named constant), and HALTS to the operator on non-convergence, NEVER auto-proceeding an un-approved PRD (unlike review's MAX_ROUNDS_DEBT which promotes+continues). (2) a GENERIC deterministic operator-decision gate primitive: `phase: awaiting-operator` + a pause object { gate, options[], context }; the sidecar notifies the orchestrator pane with the context+options and waits; the operator resumes via a single `cam resume <decision>` CLI command (thin-proxy writes the decision to the loop file; the sidecar polls, validates the decision against the active gate's options, and acts). The signal is the source of truth; the orchestrator only NARRATES. Three gates consume the primitive: plan_approval=operator (reviews the FULL audited PRD; approve->commit+branch+flip, reject->halt to idle+notify), in-progress-work conflict (detect prd.json with a passes:false non-operator story OR being on a cam/* branch; options continue->phase:implementing, abandon->deterministic clean (rm handoff.json + discard prd/branch state)+proceed, ship->delegate /cam-ship to the orchestrator in Half B, becoming phase:shipping when CAM-149 lands), and BLOCK-non-convergence. (3) reduce cam-plan.md (254 lines / 10 steps) to a thin phase-signal + narration stub (all control-flow now in TS); subagent-planner.md/subagent-auditor.md prompts UNCHANGED. Depends on CAM-117 Half A (shipped). Foundation of CAM-139 (inter-cycle drainer); the generic gate primitive is reused by CAM-149 (ship-runner) and CAM-139 (kill-switch).
acceptanceCriteria: The `.claude/cam-loop.local.md` loop file uses a `phase` enum (idle|planning|implementing|awaiting-operator|shipping) as the single source of truth; the `active` bool is DERIVED from `phase === 'implementing'` and every existing readActive/outer-loop-gate consumer reads the derived value (no independent `active` field). [oracle: bun test + grep readActive]

The sidecar outer loop detects `phase: planning` (+ plan_issue) on an idle tick and invokes runPlanPhase deterministically, mirroring the `active:true`->implement gate; no orchestrator-LLM markdown interpretation in the plan path. [oracle: bun test with injected loop file]

`cam plan N` (CLI thin-proxy) writes `phase: planning` + plan_issue to the loop file instead of injecting the /cam-plan markdown flow; a no-plannable/invalid issue halts clean, not a crash. [oracle: bun test]

On auditor APPROVE + plan_approval=auto (decidePostAuditAction/readPlanApproval, CAM-109), the runner commits the PRD + creates the branch + flips `phase: implementing`; the existing loop.ts assumes implement->review->ship->merge. [oracle: bun test]

On auditor BLOCK, a deterministic re-plan loop re-spawns the planner with the auditor findings (read from plan-verdict-report.json) injected into its prompt (CAM-37 mirror), capped at 2 rounds via a named constant; mirrors loop.ts FIXES_PENDING->re-implement. [oracle: bun test]
On re-plan non-convergence (cap hit and still BLOCK), the runner HALTS to the operator via the generic gate and NEVER auto-branches/flips an un-approved PRD. [oracle: bun test]

A generic operator-decision gate primitive exists: `phase: awaiting-operator` + a pause object { gate, options[], context }; on pause the sidecar notifies the orchestrator pane with the context + options and waits (does not auto-decide). [oracle: bun test]

`cam resume <decision>` (a single CLI command) writes the decision to the loop file; the sidecar validates it against the ACTIVE gate's options (rejecting invalid decisions with a clear error) and resumes deterministically. [oracle: bun test]

plan_approval=operator gate: on APPROVE in operator mode the runner pauses via the generic gate with the FULL audited PRD summary as context (options approve/reject); approve->commit+branch+flip phase:implementing, reject->halt to phase:idle + notify. [oracle: bun test]

In-progress-work conflict is detected deterministically at runPlanPhase start (prd.json with a passes:false non-operator story OR being on a cam/* branch) and escalated via the generic gate with options continue/ship/abandon; continue->phase:implementing, abandon->deterministic clean (rm handoff.json + discard prd/branch state)+proceed, ship->delegate /cam-ship to the orchestrator (becomes phase:shipping when CAM-149 lands). [oracle: bun test]

cam-plan.md is reduced to a thin phase-signal + narration stub (both copies: .claude/commands/ + templates/commands/, plus the embed regenerated); the 10-step control-flow is gone (now in runPlanPhase); subagent-planner.md and subagent-auditor.md prompts are unchanged. [oracle: grep + bun run embed-vendor:check + bun test]

Spawn invariants preserved for planner/auditor re-spawns: env -u CLAUDECODE (CAM-43), lowercase --session-id (CAM-23), atomic send-keys (CAM-55), mutex 1 worker-pane (CAM-55, now covering plan-phase spawns too, mutually exclusive with the implement loop via the phase enum). [oracle: bun test]

Deterministic units tested with injectable spawnFn/clock: phase transitions (planning->implementing/awaiting-operator/shipping/idle), re-plan cap + halt, gate pause/resume/validate, in-progress detection. bun run check:all passes. [oracle: bun run check:all]
ADR records the phase-enum loop state machine + the generic operator-decision gate (extend ADR 0004 or add ADR 0005, following the 0003/0004 format). [oracle: file-assert]
gotchas: SPLIT AT PLAN TIME (jobSize-3+, will overflow the 3-round review cap; mirrors CAM-117/CAM-111): B-1 = MAKE-LIVE (phase enum + active-derives-from-phase + wire runPlanPhase into the sidecar outer loop for the auto/happy path + `cam plan N` signal-writer + cam-plan.md thin stub; keep Half A's escalate-to-operator on BLOCK, NO auto re-plan yet). B-2 = GATES (generic operator-decision gate primitive + `cam resume` + BLOCK->re-plan loop + plan_approval=operator full-PRD gate + in-progress-work conflict gate). File the deferred half as a stage:idea follow-up via /cam-issue BEFORE branching (keeps the CAM-121 guard clean).

REBUILD-GATE: unlike CAM-117 Half A (inert, runPlanPhase uncalled), B-1 WIRES runPlanPhase into the live sidecar path. After B-1 ships, rebuild+reinstall+restart the sidecar (rm -f ~/.local/bin/cam; bash scripts/build-release.sh --install; kill $(cat .claude/.cam-sidecar.pid); nohup cam sidecar >> .claude/cam-supervisor.log 2>&1 & echo $! > .claude/.cam-sidecar.pid; disown) BEFORE relying on the deterministic plan phase, since the plan-phase behavior changes from orchestrator-markdown-driven to sidecar-driven.

The phase-enum refactor crosses the 'do not rewrite runSupervisor' incremental boundary of the CAM-117 arc: `active` now DERIVES from `phase`. Keep runSupervisor's implement->review->ship logic intact; only change how the `active` gate is sourced (readActive derives from phase).

Design the operator-decision gate primitive GENERIC (gate discriminator + options[] + context), not plan-specific: CAM-149 (ship-runner pauses) and CAM-139 (drainer kill-switch/notify-on-stop) reuse the exact same 'sidecar pauses, notifies, waits for cam resume' primitive.

The split decision (oversized PRD) is NOT a new mechanism: it falls out of auditor-flags-oversized -> re-plan loop -> halt-to-operator-on-non-convergence, at which point the operator splits manually (as done for CAM-117). Do not build dedicated split logic.
plan_approval=operator now reviews the FULL AUDITED PRD (not the pre-PRD sketch of today's cam-plan.md Step 6): a deliberate behavior change for determinism.

No file-based operator-approval/pause pattern exists in the codebase today (host.ts makeNotifyOrchestrator only pushes send-keys lines); the generic gate primitive creates the first one. The orchestrator's /cam-plan (thin stub) and the CLI `cam plan` must converge on writing the same phase signal.
